Definition: A unique document ID that identifies the document in the ProQuest database. When working with the document in TDM Studio, this is also the XML filename.
The title of the document.
Example: To Electrify the United States, We’re Going to Need a Lot More Electricity

Definition: The publication date of the document in the format YYYY-MM-DD.
The source type of the document is one way that the document is categorized as part of the aggregation process.
Example: Web Resources, Newspapers, Historical Newspapers, Scholarly Journals

Definition: Information on the name of the author(s). Author's name in last name, first name format. There can be more than one author per document.
A unique number to identify the publication. Note that this is different from the document-level GOID above.
The title of the publication.
The city location of the publisher. Note that publisher location doesn't always reflect the city that the newspaper covers.
The province, state, etc. of the location of the publisher.
ISBN
The name of the publisher.
The ZipCode of the publisher.
The object type of the document.
The language of the document.
Total page count of the document.
The start page of a document. May be missing in some newspapers and could vary by newspaper title.
The name of the company(s) associated with the document. There can be more than one company associated with the document. These terms are generated by an automated system as well as editorial work.
The NAIC code(s) of the company(s) associated with the document. There can be more than one company associated with the document.
For a dissertation or thesis, the name of the candidate's advisor; Advisor's name in last name, first name format. This may not be complete. There can be more than one advisor per document.
For a dissertation or thesis, the name of the candidate's committee member. Member's name in last name, first name format. There can be more than one committee member per document.
The year that the degree was awarded.
The name of the degree awarded--this is provided from the author or based on editorial review.
The type of the degree awarded--this is provided from the author or based on editorial review.
The name of the university granting the degree.
ProQuest provided codes to identify the university granting the degree.
Location of the university that is granting the degree.
The department of the university that is granting the degree.
The PQDT Classification (Dissertation Subject) from a controlled vocabulary. There can be more than one class term per document.

These are general subject term(s) which are added by ProQuest/Clarivate via automated indexing systems and editorial efforts. These are from potentially multiple controlled thesauri. There can be more than one subject term per document.
Paper categories are broader subject categories which are added using automated indexing systems to dissertations and theses.  There can be more than one paper category per document.
Keywords which are added to the document (dissertation or thesis) by the author or an editor. These are not from a controlled vocabulary. There can also be more than one paper keyword per document.
